SIX-BOX: (1) PRIOR: filtered-DC (fbp(Rx-g)) is the sparse-view lever; 20-min K-sweep saturated at K=30 -> hr 0.4345 @ 13 params (CHAMPION). iter-12 diagnostic (K=40, 50-min, 10ep) gave only 0.368 -- CONFIRMS depth saturated ~K30 (alpha collapsed to 0.006). So depth is done; the climb toward VN 0.63 now needs CAPACITY. (2) FAILURE MODE: the 13-param bilateral gate lacks the learned-filter capacity VN uses to reach 0.63; it can preserve edges but not learn rich streak-removing priors. (3) ONE KNOB: reg_type bilateral->foe with bilateral_on_top=True at a SMALL FoE geometry (nf8/k5/nb11 = 300 reg params; total ~312 with alpha). All else byte-for-byte iter-11 (filtered-DC K=30, 20-min wall). FoE zero-init RBF => FoE(x)=0 at init AND bilateral gains zero-init => pipeline == the 0.4345 champion BYTE-FOR-BYTE at init (worst case == 0.4345, NO regression). (4) HYPOTHESIS: a small learned FoE filter bank (the mechanism that gets VN to 0.63) added to the filtered-DC unroll gives the prox genuine streak-removing capacity -> hr climbs past 0.4345 toward the VN regime, at ~312 params (still ~30x fewer than VN's 9k). Kept SMALL (300p) so it trains within the ~6 epochs K=30 allows in 20 min. (5) BUDGET: K=30 filtered + small FoE (nf8/k5 is CHEAP per step), train_n=200, max_train_s=1080, --time=00:30:00, 200-val -> 20-min budget, comparable to all solvers. (6) SERIAL; iter-14 self-dispatches (next: if FoE capacity helps, GROW nf/nb along the params-vs-hr frontier; if not, directional streak-reg instead)., dc_mode=filtered, per_step_alpha=False, foe_rbf_init_std=0.0
